exclude: 6 parts: Cherryland, Jellyland, Pipeland and others
elsewhere: 6 parts: Cherryland, Jellyland, Pipeland and others

comments.text: The game's entry point. The stack-page copier jumps here once `game` is in memory and its top half has been copied to $B100-$FFFF; it jumps on to the start-up at $196C.
Interrupt exit for when the KERNAL is switched out: pulls Y, X and A pushed by $1862 and returns. $1884 makes the dispatcher at $1868 leave through here.

Installs the front-end raster interrupt with the CIA interrupts off. A goes to $01; X/Y (the routine to call each interrupt) go into the operand of the JSR at $1875. Carry clear puts $1868 in both $0314 and $FFFE, carry set $1862, so it works with the KERNAL in or out. The exit jump at $1881 is set back to $EA7E; the raster interrupt is enabled at line $F9 and CIA 1 timer A stopped.
Entry used when the KERNAL is switched out: pushes A, X and Y as the KERNAL's own entry would have, then falls into $1868.

Front-end raster interrupt. If the VIC raised it: acknowledges it, calls the routine in the JSR at $1875 (set by $1809), writes the A it returns to $D012 as the next line and the X/Y it returns back into that JSR as the next routine. Leaves through the JMP at $1881: $EA7E, the KERNAL's register restore, or $1803 when the KERNAL is out.
Points the dispatcher's exit jump ($1881) at $1803, the game's own register restore, for when the KERNAL is switched out.
Points the dispatcher's exit jump ($1881) back at the KERNAL's $EA7E.

Raster handler: next link $22E9 at line $FA; $18D3 waits in the NOP slide, turns extended colour mode on ($19C2), places sprites 3 and 4 and colours sprites 0-5 white, sets the sprite pointers at $47FA/$4BFA and $47FE-$47FF/$4BFE-$4BFF, and clears X expansion and the background colours $D021-$D023.

Start-up. Switches the BASIC and KERNAL ROMs out ($01 = $35), keeps the current raster line in $1B42, calls $BBA6, writes $C1 into the low byte of the NMI vector at $0318, selects VIC bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) through CIA 2 port A, sets screen $4400 and characters $7800 ($19AA), sets the CIA 1 port directions for the keyboard and stick ($19A0), runs $3F52, then jumps to the protection screen at $4400.
CIA 1 port B as input, port A as output.
$D018 = $1F: screen $4400, characters $7800 in bank 1.
$D018 = $2F: screen $4800, characters $7800 in bank 1.
Clears $D011 bit 6, extended colour mode.
Disables every sprite, then sets extended colour mode ($19C2).
Sets $D011 bit 6, extended colour mode.
Clears $D011 bit 4, blanking the screen.
Sets $D016 bit 4, multicolour mode.
Clears $D016 bit 4.
$D016 with the fine scroll 0 and 40 columns (bit 3).
Fills $43C0-$43FE with A.
Zeroes every sprite position register.
Background and border black.
Fills the colour RAM $D800-$DBE7 with A and both screens, $4400-$4BE7, with X (each stored into the operand of a load in the loop first).
Switches to $01 = $35: RAM everywhere but the I/O chips. $1A51 is the same without the SEI.
Sets the sprite chip's shared registers (multicolours $D025/$D026, priority, multicolour mode, X and Y expansion, X high bits, enable) from eight six-entry tables at $1A87-$1AB1, entry X.

Reads joystick port 2 ($DC00) once and spreads its five bits over $1BDE-$1BE2 (up, down, left, right, fire): each byte keeps only its own bit, so 0 means pressed. The value read lands in the operand at $1AC5, the mask in $1AC7.
Writes A to $DC00 to select keyboard rows, returns the column bits from $DC01 once two reads agree, then deselects ($1AE1).
Writes $7F to both CIA 1 ports.
Inverts every byte of $7800-$7FFF (EOR #$FF), the character set's 2 KB.
Set to 1 by the raster interrupt each frame ($2088); the play loop at $1E9B waits for it and decrements it, so a pass of the game runs at most once a frame.

The top of the play loop. Waits for the frame flag $1B3B and decrements it, deselects the keyboard ($1AE1). While paused ($1BC5) it only reads keyboard row 7 for Q (column 6): Q sets $CF81 to $FF and jumps to $3B3F with A = $1BEC. Otherwise reads the stick ($1AB7) and runs the pass.
Common head of every handler in the play-time raster chain: saves A, X and Y in zero page $0C-$0E and acknowledges the raster interrupt.
Sets the next link of the play-time raster chain: A is the raster line, X/Y the handler's address, written straight into the hardware vector $FFFE/$FFFF (the KERNAL is switched out in play).
Common tail of the play-time raster chain: restores A, X and Y from $0C-$0E and returns from the interrupt.

One frame of horizontal scroll. Subtracts the operand at $208C (the scroll speed) from the fine scroll in $10 and keeps its low three bits. When it passes a character, steps the coarse column $0F one way or the other by $1B3F (0-39, wrapping with $1BDD set to $27 and $1B48 incremented) and sets $1B3C. Then, unless $1BC9 is set, sets the frame flag $1B3B.

Sets the background colour $D021. While the counter in the operand at $20E2 runs (counting down unless $1B68 is set), the colour comes from the table at $BE38 until an entry with bit 7 set; otherwise from the operand at $20F3.

The handler that ends the frame's raster chain: sets the next interrupt to $213D at line $2F, runs $C0DC, sets both character multicolours to the operands at $2108/$210D, sets the background colour ($20E1), then the border: colour from the operand at $211A when $1C19 is 0, otherwise $B293 when $1BC9 is negative, or else the panel ($E426) and, when $1BD1 is set, $B312. Always ends with $BDD7.

First half of a double interrupt that lands the next one on an exact cycle. Saves A, Y and X in the operands of the loads at $21AE-$21B3 and the stack pointer in the operand at $21A7, sets the next interrupt for line $30 at $2162, re-enables interrupts and runs into the NOP slide at $B17A, where the second interrupt arrives with at most a cycle of jitter.

Second half: VSP, the trick that scrolls the playfield sideways without moving a character. Patches its own JSR at $2196 to enter the NOP slide at $B182 + coarse column/2 ($0F, 0-39), sets the fine scroll from $10 with multicolour on, waits in the slide, then writes $12 and $1B to $D011 on line $30: the bad line starts late by that many cycles, and the video chip draws the whole screen shifted by as many characters. Sets the next handler ($21EE at line $52), restores the stack pointer and registers saved by $213D, and sets $D018 from the operand at $21AA.
Raster handler: next link $2210 at line $72. Stores X (0 here) in $1BA9 unless $1B7F is set, calls $C0DB, and $BA08 while $1BC9 is 0.
Raster handler: next link $2222 at line $92; calls $C0DB.

Raster handler: next link $229C at line $B2; calls $C0DB. Then reads the pause key unless $1BD1 is set or $208C is 8. With the stick centred and RUN/STOP down ($DC01 bit 7) it pauses: $1BC5 = 1, $1BD7 kept in $1BD8 and $208C in $2295, both zeroed, and $0D1B called. While paused, RUN/STOP released with the stick moved resumes and restores $1BD7 and $208C ($FF). Ends through the scroll step at $2088.
Raster handler: next link $22BA at line $D2; stores $FF in $1BA9, calls $C0DB, and $F07E while $1B3E is 0.

Raster handler: next link $18C1 at line $EE; calls $BAC3 and $349C, then sets the low byte of $18D3's JSR into the NOP slide from the table at $3483, indexed by sprite 7's Y position when it is between $DA and $F1 (0 otherwise).
A run of NOPs. $213D waits in it for the second interrupt; $2162 enters it at $B182 + column/2 to time the VSP write; $18D3 and $1370 enter it at other points as delays.
